clinician.trajectory_summary: A 16-year-old male presented with acute hemorrhagic manifestations (diffuse petechial rash, bilateral subconjunctival hemorrhages, hemoptysis) on a background of several months of constitutional symptoms (fatigue, bone pain, night sweats). Initial CBC showed severe leukocytosis (WBC 101 × 10^9/L), anemia (hemoglobin 106 g/L), and thrombocytopenia (platelets 12 × 10^9/L). Peripheral blood smear revealed 75% leukemic blasts. Initial cytogenetic analysis identified Burkitt leukemia with MYC rearrangement (85% of cells) and karyotype 46,XY,dup(1)(q12q43~44),t(8;14)(q24.1;q32). The patient received chemotherapy for Burkitt leukemia. Seven months after completion of initial therapy, a bone marrow aspirate showed marked hypercellularity with significant eosinophilia and absence of elevated blasts, consistent with a myeloproliferative disorder. Whole-genome sequencing (22X depth on Illumina HiSeqX) and RNAseq (294X depth on Illumina HiSeq 2500) of this MPN bone marrow sample identified a 600 kb dispersed duplication from ABL1 to PRRC2B (9q34) inserted into the ETV6 locus (12p13). RNAseq analysis confirmed the presence of an ETV6-ABL1 fusion transcript with an intact, in-frame ABL tyrosine kinase domain. Notably, whole-genome sequencing of the initial Burkitt leukemia sample did not show evidence of the ETV6-ABL1 fusion. The patient was treated with imatinib (tyrosine kinase inhibitor) and subsequently underwent a 10/10 matched unrelated hematopoietic stem cell transplant. He achieved disease-free status and remains disease-free five years post-transplant.

evaluation.known_final_diagnosis: Whole-genome sequencing of his MPN BMA sample was performed on an Illumina HiSeqX platform with a depth of 22X, and RNAseq was performed on Illumina HiSeq 2500, with a depth of 294X. Structural variant analysis from whole-genome sequencing showed a dispersed duplication event of approximately 600 kb from ABL1 to PRRC2B (9q34), inserted into the ETV6 locus (12p13) (Figure 2, right panel). RNAseq analysis confirmed the presence of a corresponding ETV6-ABL1 fusion transcript, with an intact, in-frame ABL tyrosine–kinase domain.
